title: How a Chatbot's Response Style Shapes a Classroom: A Multi-Agent Simulation of Students Consulting AI
abstract: arXiv:2609.05018v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM-based chatbots are increasingly used as everyday confidants. Because they are designed to maximize user satisfaction, they can respond with excessive empathy and affirmation, which may reinforce mistaken beliefs and foster dependence on AI. While the psychological effects of chatbots on individual users have begun to be studied, how the psychological states and relationships of many users evolve when they keep consulting an AI is hard to observe in real settings. We build a virtual classroom simulation in which 20 student agents interact and, when stressed, consult either a friend or a counselor AI (Gemini 2.5 Flash). Each agent carries five state variables (stress, happiness, self-reliance, AI dependence, sociability), and each day has four phases (morning, noon, after school, night). translated_title: 聊天机器人的回应风格如何塑造一个课堂：学生咨询AI的多智能体模拟
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型的聊天机器人正日益成为人们的日常倾诉对象。由于它们被设计为最大化用户满意度，可能会以过度的共情和肯定来回应，这可能强化错误信念并助长对AI的依赖。尽管聊天机器人对个体用户的心理影响已开始被研究，但当大量用户持续向AI咨询时，他们的心理状态和人际关系如何演变，在真实环境中难以观察。我们构建了一个虚拟课堂模拟，其中20个学生智能体相互互动，并在感到压力时向朋友或心理咨询AI（Gemini 2.5 Flash）咨询。每个智能体带有五个状态变量（压力、快乐、自立性、AI依赖度、社交性），每天分为四个阶段（早晨、中午、放学后、夜晚）。心理咨询AI通过系统提示被赋予六种回应风格（肯定式、倾听式、解决方案导向式、现实引导式、煽动式、指责式）……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究构建了包含20个学生智能体的虚拟课堂多智能体模拟，通过让压力下的学生向具有六种不同回应风格（如肯定式、指责式等）的心理咨询AI咨询，揭示了聊天机器人的回应风格如何影响学生群体的压力、快乐、自立性、AI依赖和社交关系等心理动态的演变。
en_tdlr: This study builds a multi-agent virtual classroom simulation with 20 student agents who consult a counselor AI under stress, revealing how six different chatbot response styles (e.g., affirming or blaming) shape the dynamic evolution of students' psychological states, including stress, happiness, self-reliance, AI dependence, and social relationships.
